name: Superorder
oneLiner: AI agent platform for restaurant chains (formerly Forward Kitchens) covering review management, surveys and guest feedback, delivery profitability, scorecards and alerts.
bestFor: Multi-unit restaurant brands with significant delivery and takeout volume that want AI-written review replies across Google, Yelp and delivery apps, plus feedback flows that win back unhappy guests.

updates.text: Turning Point Restaurants, with 32 locations on the East Coast, partnered with Superorder to gather post-order feedback, manage reviews across channels and flag friction points.
L&L Hawaiian Barbecue partnered with Superorder to improve guest engagement and feedback collection across its 230+ locations.

features: Review Management Agent that answers reviews on Google, Yelp and delivery platforms from one dashboard

AI-written review replies personalized with the guest's order details (items, delivery time, errors, order history), varied by star rating and by customer segment (loyalty, average order value, order frequency)
Surveys & Feedback Agent that sends AI-driven surveys after orders to surface issues before they become public reviews
Automated recovery offers (tailored compensation) sent to dissatisfied guests
Delivery profitability agents for third-party delivery: real-time alerts, consolidated reporting, financial reconciliation and downtime tracking
AI scorecards comparing performance across locations
Insights and real-time alerts on guest issues, trends and sentiment

pricing.text: Custom pricing: one Enterprise Plan, quoted after a demo ('store-based pricing'), billed monthly on the first of the month. No free trial; a 30-day money-back guarantee instead. The plan lists unlimited users, a dedicated account manager, 1:1 onboarding, a 24-hour support response SLA, role-based access control and advanced reporting.

notes: Renamed from Forward Kitchens in 2023, when it raised a $10M Series A led by Foundation Capital (TechCrunch, Sep 2023). It has since moved from a delivery/takeout operating system and virtual storefronts to AI agents for reputation and delivery profitability. The current review's mention of 'online ordering' as part of the platform reflects the older positioning; the current product pages emphasize review, feedback and delivery-profitability agents, so leave online ordering out. The L&L partnership appears on superorder.com/press; the July 2025 date comes from a third-party company profile (yespress.io/superorder) and could not be confirmed on the press page itself. Wow Bao and Marco's Pizza are listed as restaurant partners on Superorder's Y Combinator profile, not in published case studies. Dropped vendor stats: 'won back 21% of unhappy customers' (Tasty Restaurant Group case study headline, vendor claim) and 'revisit rates up 20%' (third-party listing). No 2026 product announcements found. November 2026: pricing page read (Enterprise Plan only, quote after demo, 30-day money-back guarantee). The homepage shows logos of large chains (Pizza Hut, Wendy's, Applebee's and others) without stories; not used as customers. Homepage claims ('6M+ annual reviews processed', '11%+ survey response rates', '7x retention') are vendor claims, not used. No G2 listing found, so no rating.
pros: Replies draw on the guest's order details, so each response refers to the actual meal or delivery
Covers delivery-app reviews and third-party delivery profitability with one vendor
Post-order surveys and automated recovery offers catch unhappy guests before they post publicly
Enterprise plan includes unlimited users, a dedicated account manager and a 24-hour support response SLA

cons.text: No published prices; a quote comes after a demo
No free trial; a 30-day money-back guarantee instead
Built around delivery and takeout for multi-unit chains, so a dine-in independent may pay for agents it won't use

plans.note: One Enterprise Plan with custom pricing; 30-day money-back guarantee
